Note::TexAccessor::strip_envs¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::strip_envs() const

Remove Complete Environment Regions¶

strip_envs() removes every complete \begin{name}...\end{name} region, regardless of the environment name. It is the broad counterpart to strip_env(name): use the named form when one structural kind must disappear and unrelated environments must survive; use strip_envs() when the desired result is prose outside all complete environments.

The parser balances a stack of environment names. Consequently, nested regions with different names and same-name recursion are consumed as one outer region, rather than stopping at the first \end{...}. Names are lexical TeX names: ASCII letters and @, with an optional terminal *. An end tag closes only the matching top-of-stack name. Escaped openers are ordinary text, and an unclosed outer region is retained in full; broad cleanup never treats the end of a cell as an implied close.

Each cell is processed independently. Deleted regions leave one separator, then ASCII whitespace is collapsed and the result is trimmed. The returned Text Note has the receiver’s exact rank and shape, including cells that become empty. The method is out-of-place and idempotent. Undefined input propagates; defined Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes Notes reject. The scan is linear in the number of source bytes, with stack memory proportional to nesting depth.

Example 1: Mixed Nesting, Multiple Regions, And Malformed Source¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(A \begin{quote}outer \begin{emph}inner\end{emph} tail\end{quote} B)",
    R"(C \begin{proof}one\end{proof} D \begin{lemma}two\end{lemma} E)",
    R"(\\begin{proof}escaped\end{proof} \begin{proof}unfinished)"});
std::cout << source.tex().strip_envs() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["A B", "C D E", "\\\\begin{proof}escaped\\end{proof} \\begin{proof}unfinished"]

The nested emph region belongs to the outer quote region, both complete regions in the second lane are removed, and neither escaped nor incomplete syntax is guessed away.

Example 2: Matrices Keep Empty Cells¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{R"(x \begin{a}1\end{a} y)", "plain",
                             R"(\begin{b}2\end{b})", ""},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto clean = grid.tex().strip_envs();
std::cout << clean << '\n';
std::cout << "shape=[" << clean.size(0) << ", " << clean.size(1) << "]\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "idempotent=" << ((clean == clean.tex().strip_envs()).all().bool_item())
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["x y", "plain"], 
  ["", ""]
]
shape=[2, 2]
idempotent=true

Example 3: Undefined And Invalid Dtype¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().strip_envs().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().strip_envs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "strip envs Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
strip envs Int64: rejected
